verses.1: At that time Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem approached Jesus, saying,
verses.2: "Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? Look, they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
verses.3: But he replied to them, "Why do you also break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
verses.4: For God said, Honor your father and your mother, and, Whoever curses father or mother must die;
verses.5: but you say, If anyone says to their father or mother, Whatever benefit you have received from me
verses.6: is a gift to God, then they do not need to honor their father. In this way you have nullified the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
verses.7: Hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy about you when he said,
verses.8: This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me;
verses.9: they worship me in vain, teaching doctrines of human beings."
verses.10: Then, summoning the crowd, he said to them, "Hear and understand:
verses.11: It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth — this defiles a person."
verses.12: Then the disciples approached him and said, "You know that the Pharisees heard this teaching and took offense."
verses.13: But he replied, "Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
verses.14: Let them alone; blind guides lead the blind, and both will fall into a pit."
verses.15: Peter responded, "Explain to us this parable."
verses.16: He said, "You still do not understand either?
verses.17: Do you not realize that everything that enters the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled out?
verses.18: But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and it is this that defiles a person.
verses.19: For from the heart come evil thoughts — murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
verses.20: These are the things that defile a person, but it is not the act of eating with unwashed hands that defiles."
verses.21: Then Jesus left there and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
verses.22: A Canaanite woman from those parts came out and cried out to him, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is greatly tormented by a demon."
verses.23: But he did not answer her at all. His disciples came and asked him, "Send her away, for she is calling out after us."
verses.24: He answered, "I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
verses.25: But the woman approached and fell at his feet, saying, "Lord, help me!"
verses.26: He answered, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
verses.27: She said, "Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters."
verses.28: Then Jesus replied to her, "Woman, your faith is great. Let it be done for you as you wish." And from that hour her daughter was healed.
verses.29: Then Jesus left there and came to the Sea of Galilee, and he went up on the mountain and sat down there.
verses.30: Many crowds came to him carrying the deaf, the blind, the lame, the mute, and many others. They threw them at his feet, and he healed them.
verses.31: So the crowd was amazed as they saw the mute speaking, the lame walking, the blind seeing, and the deaf hearing, and they praised the God of Israel.
verses.32: Jesus summoned the disciples and said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because they have been with me three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way."
verses.33: His disciples said to him, "Where in the wilderness can we get so many loaves to feed such a large crowd?"
verses.34: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
verses.35: Then he told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
verses.36: He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
verses.37: They all ate and were satisfied, and the leftover fragments they gathered filled seven baskets.
verses.38: Those who ate were four thousand men, not counting women and children.
verses.39: Then, after dismissing the crowd, he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.

notes:
Notes
- v. 21: "region of Tyre and Sidon" — the Greek uses "μέρη" (parts), here rendered as "region."
- v. 22: "Canaanite woman" — the Greek "Χαναναία" is a woman of the region of Canaan; "Canaanite" is the standard reading.
- v. 26: "children's bread" — the Greek "τέκνων" is translated as "children's" to reflect the metaphor.
- v. 27: "crumbs" — the Greek "ψιχίων" is best understood as "crumbs," consistent with the metaphor of table scraps for dogs.
- v. 38: "four thousand men" — the Greek "τετρακισχίλιοι" is rendered as "four thousand" to match the numerical structure.

[1] At that time Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem approached Jesus, saying,
[2] "Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? Look, they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
[3] But he replied to them, "Why do you also break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
[4] For God said, Honor your father and your mother, and, Whoever curses father or mother must die;
[5] but you say, If anyone says to their father or mother, Whatever benefit you have received from me
[6] is a gift to God, then they do not need to honor their father. In this way you have nullified the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
[7] Hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy about you when he said,
[8] This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me;
[9] they worship me in vain, teaching doctrines of human beings."
[10] Then, summoning the crowd, he said to them, "Hear and understand:
[11] It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth — this defiles a person."
[12] Then the disciples approached him and said, "You know that the Pharisees heard this teaching and took offense."
[13] But he replied, "Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
[14] Let them alone; blind guides lead the blind, and both will fall into a pit."
[15] Peter responded, "Explain to us this parable."
[16] He said, "You still do not understand either?
[17] Do you not realize that everything that enters the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled out?
[18] But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and it is this that defiles a person.
[19] For from the heart come evil thoughts — murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
[20] These are the things that defile a person, but it is not the act of eating with unwashed hands that defiles."
[21] Then Jesus left there and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
[22] A Canaanite woman from those parts came out and cried out to him, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is greatly tormented by a demon."
[23] But he did not answer her at all. His disciples came and asked him, "Send her away, for she is calling out after us."
[24] He answered, "I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
[25] But the woman approached and fell at his feet, saying, "Lord, help me!"
[26] He answered, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
[27] She said, "Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters."
[28] Then Jesus replied to her, "Woman, your faith is great. Let it be done for you as you wish." And from that hour her daughter was healed.
[29] Then Jesus left there and came to the Sea of Galilee, and he went up on the mountain and sat down there.
[30] Many crowds came to him carrying the deaf, the blind, the lame, the mute, and many others. They threw them at his feet, and he healed them.
[31] So the crowd was amazed as they saw the mute speaking, the lame walking, the blind seeing, and the deaf hearing, and they praised the God of Israel.
[32] Jesus summoned the disciples and said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because they have been with me three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way."
[33] His disciples said to him, "Where in the wilderness can we get so many loaves to feed such a large crowd?"
[34] Jesus asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
[35] Then he told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
[36] He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
[37] They all ate and were satisfied, and the leftover fragments they gathered filled seven baskets.
[38] Those who ate were four thousand men, not counting women and children.
[39] Then, after dismissing the crowd, he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
